description: VM 118 — db-postgres-18 (192.168.20.23, pg18.internal.prakash.com.br). Guest CPU, memory, disk and network pressure alongside PostgreSQL health and the shared Proxmox pve/data thin pool. Uses the existing pg18 node-exporter and postgres-exporter targets; no database selector changes the VM-wide totals.

panels.description: node_exporter availability on VM 118 (192.168.20.23). UNAVAILABLE means the scrape failed or its series is missing; it does not by itself prove the VM is powered off.
panels.title: Host metrics

panels.description: OK requires a successful exporter scrape, pg_up=1 and no exporter collection error. Missing metrics are shown as unavailable.
panels.title: PostgreSQL health

panels.description: Time since the guest booted. This is VM uptime, not the age of the PostgreSQL process.
panels.title: VM uptime

panels.description: Memory unavailable to new allocations, using MemAvailable so reclaimable filesystem cache is not counted as exhausted RAM.
panels.title: Memory used

panels.description: Space available to PostgreSQL on /data, which contains /data/postgresql/18_main. The Proxmox pve/data pool is a separate capacity limit shown below.
panels.title: Database disk free

panels.description: Client backends as a share of the cluster-wide max_connections budget, including idle pooled connections. Autovacuum and parallel workers have separate process budgets and are excluded.
panels.title: Connections used

panels.description: Average across all vCPUs. I/O wait and steal are shown separately from execution; guest modes are excluded because Linux already includes them in user/nice time.
panels.title: CPU time by mode

panels.description: Used is MemTotal minus MemAvailable. Available includes memory the kernel can reclaim; the dashed line is the VM total.
panels.title: Memory available and used

panels.description: Linux load averages divided by the number of vCPUs. A value above 1 means more runnable or uninterruptible tasks than CPUs; I/O waits also contribute to load.
panels.title: Load per vCPU

panels.description: Percentage of wall time in which at least one task waited for CPU, memory or I/O (PSI some). I/O full means all non-idle tasks were stalled together. These series overlap and are not stacked.
panels.title: Task stalls (PSI)
Guest storage — sda: system, sdb: PostgreSQL data

panels.description: Bytes available to applications on the root filesystem and PostgreSQL data disk. The separate backing thin pool is shown at the bottom of this dashboard.
panels.title: Filesystem free space

panels.description: Allocated or reserved space as a share of each filesystem, plus inode usage. Temporary filesystems and the EFI partition are excluded.
panels.title: Filesystem space and inodes used

panels.description: Bytes read and written per second on the system (sda) and data (sdb) disks, averaged over five minutes.
panels.title: Disk throughput

panels.description: Average completion time per read or write as observed by the guest. This is not query latency or a percentile. A direction with no completed operations has no latency sample.
panels.title: Average I/O latency

panels.description: Completed disk operations per second, split by device and direction.
panels.title: Disk IOPS

panels.description: Share of wall time during which each device serviced requests. SSDs can serve requests in parallel, so busy time alone does not establish saturation; compare with PSI and latency.
panels.title: Disk busy time

panels.description: Receive and transmit throughput on the VM LAN interface eth0. Loopback is excluded.
panels.title: LAN traffic

panels.description: Absolute bytes keep this panel meaningful when swap is disabled: both lines are zero, with no division by a zero capacity.
panels.title: Swap used and total

panels.description: Client backends grouped by state, excluding autovacuum and parallel workers. Idle connections still consume max_connections slots; idle in transaction can hold locks and snapshots. Open the PostgreSQL dashboard for per-database details.
panels.title: Connections by state

panels.description: Shared physical backing for the disks of VMs 112, 117 and 118, not storage used by this VM alone. Both data and metadata exhaustion can stop guest writes even when /data reports free space. Missing collector metrics remain No data.
panels.title: Proxmox pve/data thin pool
